headline: Azure for Students Activation Without University Email in 2026
summary: Microsoft's cloud platform offers $100 in credits and free services, but activation can be tricky if your university's domain isn't recognized. Here's how to get it.
details: Azure for Students provides enrolled university students with $100 in Azure credits, access to free services, and no credit card requirement. The standard activation process relies on your university email domain being registered with Microsoft, which is not the case for many institutions, particularly outside North America and Europe. If you encounter the message "your email domain is not currently registered with us," it means you need to use an alternative verification method.

Two primary alternative paths exist when your institutional domain isn't recognized: verifying with official academic documentation or using the GitHub Student Developer Pack as proof of student status. Both methods are supported by Microsoft and SheerID, the verification provider for Azure for Students. You'll need a Microsoft account to proceed, so create one at account.microsoft.com if you don't already have one.

For the academic documentation route, navigate to azure.microsoft.com/free/students and click 'Activate now.' Sign in with your Microsoft account, not your university email. When the domain isn't verified automatically, you'll be prompted to submit official enrollment documentation. This document must clearly show your full name, institution's name, and current enrollment status. A student ID card is usually insufficient.

The verification is handled by SheerID and typically completes within minutes, though it can take up to 48 hours. If verification fails after 48 hours, contact Azure Education Support. Once verified, your Azure for Students subscription, including $100 in credits valid for 12 months and access to always-free services, will appear in the Azure portal.

Alternatively, if you have or plan to get the GitHub Student Developer Pack, you can use it for verification. Apply for the Pack at education.github.com/pack, providing your university details and proof of enrollment if your email isn't recognized. GitHub's verification can take up to 72 hours. Once confirmed, proceed to signup.azure.com/studentverification and sign in with your Microsoft account to activate Azure for Students.

headline_marked: [[GrapheneOS confirms]] Pixel 11 hardware-level MTE support remains
headline: GrapheneOS confirms Pixel 11 hardware-level MTE support remains
summary: While hardware acceleration may be reduced, GrapheneOS suggests the Pixel 11 could still offer usable MTE capabilities.
details: GrapheneOS has provided an update on the Pixel 11's support for Memory Tagging Extension (MTE). Despite initial concerns, the operating system developer confirms that the Pixel 11 retains at least bare minimum hardware-level support for MTE.

It is believed that Google may have reduced hardware acceleration from the CPU cache in the Pixel 11 to cut costs. This change reportedly impacted performance, leading to the feature's full disabling in firmware.

However, GrapheneOS suggests that the underlying hardware support might still be salvageable. This could mean that while not fully optimized, the MTE functionality might still be usable on the Pixel 11.

MTE is a security feature designed to help detect and mitigate memory corruption vulnerabilities, which are common in software development. Its presence, even in a limited capacity, is crucial for enhancing device security.
